lantern_cai_tong.name: Cai Tong
lantern_cai_tong.title: Contracted driver of the ordinary association passenger cart

lantern_zheng_bao.name: Zheng Bao
lantern_zheng_bao.title: Zheng Lin's niece and household receiver

lantern_02_001.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_001.text: The Day 1391 cart reached the eastern yard while Nan's breakfast pot still steamed. Cai Tong checked its brake on the level loading strip and inspected the passenger bench restraints before calling names. The freight remained under its counted covering, with Zheng's lens case in its agreed dry place. Yue boarded after the driver directed her. She did not help by stepping between a loaded wheel and the gatepost. Qiu stood beside the accepted list until the last passenger found a seat.

lantern_02_002.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_002.text: At the bridge, the watcher checked the morning repair report and admitted the controlled lane. Cai drove at the posted walking pace. A second worker kept the crossing's far end clear. The mules' hooves sounded differently on new gravel laid over the old approach. Yue looked through the side opening at the mill race and the mason's closed foot lane. The water carried a strip of straw beneath the piers. No personal trace steadied the bridge, and the ticket purchased no exception to its actual load limit.

lantern_02_003.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_003.text: The cart stopped on firm ground beyond the bridge so Cai could inspect the harness after the confined turn. Zheng asked whether his case had shifted. Its restraint held, and the driver showed him before moving. Yue checked her own pack without unloading it into the road. The third passenger, a woman named Rui Sui, carried wrapped cloth samples for an ordinary school purchasing meeting. She kept their owners' price cards covered. The school had asked for samples, rather than every workshop's accounts.

lantern_02_004.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_004.text: Cai explained the route at the first scheduled rest. Eight travel days would reach Chime Reach under the current road reports. The association fare included seven accepted overnight bench places and the driver's ordinary meals, with passenger food separately priced by the houses. The original ticket's paid carriage amount would be settled between the receiving offices. It supplied no money for optional visits. A road closure would require the named station contact to approve actual additional arrangements; it did not turn Cai into a lodging fund.

lantern_02_005.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_005.text: Yue checked that explanation against the terms attached to her ticket. The accepted bench places were real reservations along the ordinary route. She had paid her Wheatbridge wait separately because those nights preceded the carriage. Her own food pouch covered the next stated meals. Zheng carried provisions from his household gathering. Rui had received a finite travel allowance from the school purchase budget and kept the remaining money in a cloth inside her sleeve. Different passengers had reached the same bench under different accounts.

lantern_02_006.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_006.text: The first road ran between bean fields with dark ridges of recently turned soil. Rui watched the straight rows and began counting quietly. She stopped when Cai pointed to a junction where the driver needed everyone seated. A pig cart waited there under a torn red cover. Its owner had placed an ordinary warning cone behind the stuck wheel and gone to fetch a jack. Cai used the checked outer lane. The stuck cart's inconvenience did not authorise passengers to invent a rescue with equipment they had not inspected.

lantern_02_007.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_007.text: At the next house, Cai reported the stopped cart to the route keeper with its visible location. The keeper had already received the owner's request and sent an assigned repair worker. Yue saw the second report added as confirmation, rather than credited as the first discovery. The pig owner might never know their names. The keeper's reply was enough to let Cai continue her own journey. Rui bought three boiled eggs, discovered one cracked, and exchanged it before leaving the counter. This small failure had a receiver available immediately.

lantern_02_008.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_008.text: Their Day 1391 halt was Red Sill House, built against a low sandstone bank. Its bench room had assigned places marked with removable wooden tags. Zheng's place stood near the door to shorten his night walk. Yue put her travelling source wrapper on the dry shelf within reach of her own place. She did not ask the house to guard it under an invented institutional duty. Its custody remained hers. Cai paid the carriage account's accepted overnight charge against the actual names and retained the receipt.

lantern_02_009.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_009.text: A house worker offered a separate storage cabinet for large goods. Rui declined because the cloth samples already fitted her permitted shelf. The worker had expected the samples to require a sealed chest and seemed disappointed at losing a sale. Rui explained that ordinary covers and a dry support met their present handling need. Her workshops had not funded decorative custody. Yue liked the answer but said nothing until the worker left. Rui would rather have asked about the school meeting, where cloth needed to survive children as well as shelves.

lantern_02_010.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_010.text: Zheng told them about a classroom lamp he had once repaired. The teacher wanted its shutter silent because a clicking signal distracted the pupils. He had fitted a felt stop, then discovered that the school needed the click during its fire drill. The ordinary teacher had asked for two different uses without realising they shared one piece. Zheng returned and made a removable stop under a new paid work order. He still remembered the child's blunt question about why adults called a thing improved before trying both uses.

lantern_02_011.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_011.text: Rui laughed because her purchasing request contained the same problem. The school wanted cloth dark enough to hide ink and light enough to make missing insects visible during the children's garden lessons. The sample seller had promised both qualities without showing a test. Rui planned to compare the actual samples under the classroom lamps and outdoors. A low price would matter after that comparison, not before it. Yue offered no verdict about cloth from the small wraps she had seen. Their owners had supplied a question which needed the school itself.

lantern_02_012.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_012.text: On Day 1392, low rain followed them across the upper road. Cai lowered the weather flap without closing the clear forward view. Yue could see the mule pair's ears and the driver's hand against the ordinary rein. Zheng took shorter breaths while climbing into the cart after a rest, then sat before speaking. He said the damp made his ribs remember an old illness. It was his own description, not a diagnosis Yue could repeat as an examined fact. Cai asked whether he wanted the next stop shortened.

lantern_02_013.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_013.text: He wanted the planned dry rest, which arrived before the rain strengthened. The house keeper had set a brazier outside the closed grain room and kept the visitor stools clear of its hot guard. Zheng warmed his hands there while Rui inspected her cloth covers. Yue bought hot broth from the passenger meal counter. The carriage booking did not include it, and the charge came from her food money. The receipt named broth. It did not become treatment merely because warmth made her shoulders feel less tired.

lantern_02_014.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_014.text: A courier waiting under the same eaves carried a letter for Chime's relay examiner. He knew Zheng and asked whether the old lens might be used in a public demonstration. Zheng declined for the coming week because he had already promised his niece time at home. The courier offered to say the demonstration had been requested. That was fine. He could not say it was accepted. Zheng wrote the distinction on a small message and paid the ordinary delivery charge. The cracked lens stayed inside its supported case.

lantern_02_015.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_015.text: Yue watched the courier's ordinary horse carry the message away when the route keeper admitted his lane. The lamp demonstration had acquired a real refusal before a public notice could make it look inevitable. Rui said that schools often printed a guest's name when someone merely suggested inviting the guest. Her own purchase meeting used a confirmation column. The column seemed dull until a visiting worker failed to arrive. Yue thought of the received form she had completed at Wheatbridge and wondered whether useful dullness was a skill people learned late.

lantern_02_016.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_016.text: Their second overnight house stood above a shallow flood channel. Cai checked its current approach notice before unloading the passenger bags. The lower yard was closed, while the upper entrance remained admitted for the booked cart. Rainwater ran through a recently cleared ditch beside the wheels. Yue carried her pack on the ordinary steps and used the rail the house had installed for everyone. She left her personal reserve untested. The existence of a trained reinforced stance did not create a reason to perform one on wet unfamiliar steps.

lantern_02_017.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_017.text: Inside, a traveller complained that the kitchen had watered its soup. The cook showed the recipe's ordinary bean stock and offered the posted refund for an unopened portion. His own bowl was already half empty. He decided to finish it and continued complaining while he ate. Zheng listened with a smile, then asked the cook about the dry sleeping room. That was the service he actually needed. The complaint supplied no evidence that every part of the house had failed, though the traveller seemed eager for that larger story.

lantern_02_018.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_018.text: Rui received a letter from the school purchasing clerk through the house's ordinary post desk. A classroom assistant would conduct the outdoor cloth test because the teacher's ankle had been injured. The purchasing meeting still had its appointed receiver and dates. Rui checked that the letter named the assistant's authority to accept the samples. It did. She revised her plan without asking Yue to judge the absent teacher's condition. A worker's injury had changed who performed a task, and the institution had supplied another actual person rather than an honorary title.

lantern_02_019.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_019.text: The following morning, Cai found a cracked leather keeper beside the cart's rear restraint. The load had remained held by the primary tie, but the cracked keeper could let its slack strike the wheel. She removed the faulty piece and replaced it from her inspected repair stock. Yue held the light loose strap only after Cai directed the safe position. The driver logged the replacement against her ordinary service allowance. Rui wanted to pay as a grateful passenger. Cai said the fare already funded sound ordinary carriage within its agreed scope.

lantern_02_020.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_020.text: They departed on Day 1393 after the route keeper checked the upper lane again. The road crossed a ridge where the wind moved low grass in uneven dark waves. Zheng pointed to an abandoned signal post beside the verge. It had once marked a private mill cart's turn and now stood outside the current route. Cai followed the present painted markers. Yue could admire the old post without treating it as guidance. Its former usefulness belonged to a different owner, purpose, and road condition than today's passenger journey.

lantern_02_021.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_021.text: At a market halt, Rui found a school exercise book whose binding matched one of her cloth samples. The seller permitted her to test the hinge on an ordinary display copy. Its stitching held, while the cloth near the corner frayed. Rui bought the copy for her own comparison, using a permitted incidental line in the school travel allowance. She asked for a receipt naming the actual book. The seller wanted to write classroom supplies, which would have concealed the sample. He rewrote it without argument when she explained.

lantern_02_022.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_022.text: Yue bought a small packet of dried greens for her next meal. The seller tied it in a reused wrapper printed with a relay advertisement from the previous year. Its transmission times no longer matched Deng's public sheet. Yue asked whether he had current notices. He had never received one and sold food rather than messages. She gave him the public receiving address from her admitted copy. He could request the current sheet. She did not declare his used wrapper a deliberate false instruction to customers who came for greens.

lantern_02_023.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_023.text: The seller kept the address because carriers ate at his stall. He wanted a notice he could put beside the meal board. Rui offered him no school money for printing it. Chime's association had its own correction circulation allocation, and its office would need to decide whether this actual stop belonged on that list. Yue wrote the request as a current local need with the seller's permission. It joined her future receiving questions, separate from the basin records she had carried under narrower terms.

lantern_02_024.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_024.text: That afternoon the wind loosened the cart's outer rain cover. Cai stopped before the fluttering corner could obscure her turning view. She and the route-house worker fastened it with a sound spare tie. Yue stayed on the bench, keeping Zheng's case clear of the work area. He wanted to show her a quicker old knot. Cai asked whether the knot had been tested on this material under the current load. It had not. He grinned at being corrected and held the loose corner exactly where she requested instead.

lantern_02_025.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_025.text: The third house had a small courtyard fig tree and no ripe fruit. A child charged visitors one pebble to look at the tree because somebody had once paid her to watch birds there. The house keeper stopped the charge when a passenger took it seriously. He returned the man's pebble and explained the private game. Yue asked the child what a pebble bought within the game. A promise to point at a bird, if one arrived. Yue accepted the terms and found a smooth ordinary stone by the drain.

lantern_02_026.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_026.text: No bird came before supper. The child returned the stone solemnly, then offered to show a moth for the same price. Yue declined because she wanted to eat. The game remained hers without needing to occupy every visitor. Zheng bought a pear from the real meal counter and asked the child to keep her moth away from its slice. Rui showed her the exercise book's frayed corner with the house keeper present. The child thought cloth ought to survive teeth, which added an unexpected use to Rui's already difficult purchasing question.

lantern_02_027.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_027.text: On Day 1394, they reached the district road office at Split Ash. Cai presented the cart's booking and current axle record. The clerk checked the actual loaded weight rather than assuming a familiar association cart carried its familiar contents. Zheng's practice lens and Rui's cloth samples were listed baggage. Neither became commercial freight without its owners' consent and revised carriage terms. The clerk admitted the continuation under the present passenger limit. A separate merchant's heavier cart remained waiting for its own assessment, visible through the office's side window.

lantern_02_028.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_028.text: That merchant accused the association of taking priority because its passengers knew important people. Cai showed her actual appointment slot, booked before their arrival. She offered no opinion about the clerk's other customers. Yue stayed out of the argument, though she could feel how easily her sword and stage cord might become part of the man's imagined explanation. The clerk called the next booked driver, who knew nobody at their bench. The ordinary queue supplied a clearer answer than a traveller defending every institution on the road.

lantern_02_029.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_029.text: They ate at Split Ash before leaving. The cooking shelter sold a filling meal for one copper and drinking water from its inspected municipal tank at the ordinary household rate. Cai's animal watering came from her carriage account, with the quantities on its service record. Passenger cups belonged to their meal purchases. Yue watched the keeper direct used washing water into a separate drain. The details reminded her of the basin, but she did not merge the two sources. This supply had its own keeper, dates, and current checks.

lantern_02_030.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_030.text: Zheng had brought an old sketch of the Split Ash office roof because he wanted to see whether its earlier repair lasted. He compared it from the public yard, where he could see the outer braces. A new clerk asked whether he had returned to certify the roof. He had not. The current inspection belonged to the appointed building examiner. Zheng could point to a difference and ask for the record if its owner permitted. He folded the sketch when the clerk explained that the inner repair file was not available at this public counter.

lantern_02_031.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_031.text: Later, he admitted to Yue that he disliked being told which part of his former work he no longer owned. The institution had paid him for it, and its records remained under its custody. He owned his permitted sketch and his memories. Yue asked whether he wanted to become the current examiner again. He did not. The duties would occupy more than his household could now accept. Keeping the right to refuse the job meant accepting that another person performed its decisions. He sat with that answer until the next rest.

lantern_02_032.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_032.text: At the fourth overnight house, Cai confirmed the remaining three bench reservations through the route desk. The last approach to Chime had an additional inspection after recent bank work. Its current report admitted passenger carts under a lowered pace, with a morning review. The planned arrival remained Day 1398. If that review failed, the cart would stop at the appointed house and request new actual terms. Yue checked her own food allowance. She could afford the accepted schedule and one additional purchased meal, with a personal margin still held for ordinary contingencies.

lantern_02_033.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_033.text: Rui's school letter named the purchasing sitting on Day 1400. She would have two days after the planned arrival to arrange the actual sample tests. A delay beyond that date could require a new meeting, whose authority belonged to the school. She wrote a short provisional message describing her current position and paid the post charge from the admitted travel line. The school could choose another supply while waiting, if its need required. Rui wanted the cloth accepted, but her wish could not make the classroom's deadline wait automatically.

lantern_02_034.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_034.text: Yue had no accepted Chime post awaiting her arrival. Deng's receiving address named a proposal, and its question could remain open if the road took longer. That freedom felt different from having nothing to do. She had a place to begin and duties whose permitted receivers were already named. She slept with the source wrapper safely beside her own belongings. Through the partition, somebody counted the driver's departure coins twice. Real schedules ended many days with people checking the same small sum until its shape became convincing.

lantern_02_035.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_035.text: The Day 1395 road crossed a stone causeway built above a dry seasonal channel. Its inspection post carried a recent mark and a warning about the lower shoulders. Cai kept to the admitted centre. A shepherd moved sheep behind the ordinary crossing gate and waited while the loaded cart passed. The animals looked offended by the gate's existence. Rui watched one black lamb try to climb its mother. Zheng laughed so suddenly he coughed, then waited until his breath steadied before commenting on the lamb's ambitious engineering.

lantern_02_036.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_036.text: They stopped at the next dry shelter. Cai asked Zheng whether the cough had changed from his earlier description. He wanted rest and water, with no reported chest pain or new difficulty beyond the brief spell. The local care contact was named on the shelter notice if he needed assessment. Yue could offer an ordinary cup and wait beside him because he asked. She could not promise that old symptoms remained harmless. Zheng accepted the cup, then asked whether anybody had remembered to laugh at the mother's expression too.

lantern_02_037.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_037.text: Rui received a reply through the shelter desk confirming the school's provisional handling plan. The classroom assistant could perform the outdoor comparison on Day 1399 if she arrived as expected. A later arrival would move the purchasing sitting rather than let an absent sample become approved by default. The reply supplied no compensation claim because no delay had yet occurred. Rui put it with the original offer. Its usefulness lay in making the school's next decision possible, including a decision she might not prefer.

lantern_02_038.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_038.text: At the fifth house, a rope maker shared the meal bench with them and recognised the loop on Yue's bowl cloth. He said its maker always left the return end longer than necessary. Yue asked whether that made it unsafe. It made it easier to untie, though the loose end should remain clear of a wheel. Her loop closed a bowl wrapper and carried no cart load. The rope maker tested it only with her permission and returned it. He liked finding a familiar trade decision travelling under an unfamiliar person's fingers.

lantern_02_039.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_039.text: Zheng bought a replacement cord for his lens case. The old one still held, but its worn outer fibres had begun catching on the lid. He kept the replaced piece for a household shutter rather than listing it as sound carriage restraint. The rope maker charged for the measured length and gave him the material description. Yue watched Zheng compare the new cord's thickness with the case slots. He did not choose the strongest available rope if its bulk would put pressure on the glass cover it needed to protect.

lantern_02_040.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_040.text: On Day 1396, they passed the first Chime association receiving post, though the town remained two days away by the cart road. Ma Yan's dispatcher mark appeared on a current notice beside the local keeper's name. It listed four old-relay windows and ordinary carrier alternatives. One afternoon window had been cancelled for an isolation check. Its messages would use the next admitted transmission or the priced ground route, according to the sender's actual choice. The notice did not choose for every sender merely to make the queue look shorter.

lantern_02_041.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_041.text: The post keeper asked Cai to carry two accepted public notice packets to Chime. Their small load fitted the recorded spare freight allowance after she weighed them. She signed their temporary custody under the carriage terms. Yue was not their receiver and did not add them to her own source wrapper. Rui wanted to read the cancellation detail for her school. The keeper supplied the public viewing copy. The sealed onward packets stayed intact. One useful public fact could be available without every object containing it becoming common baggage.

lantern_02_042.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_042.text: At the next rest, Yue copied the current correction address onto the food seller's request. Cai permitted her to put the request into Chime's ordinary message tray when they arrived, under the actual stated post fee. She would still need the association to accept its circulation question. The cancelled relay window had made the seller's need more concrete. Travellers could arrive at his stall carrying a schedule already superseded. The request named his actual location, rather than asking the office to distribute new sheets everywhere she imagined people ate.

lantern_02_043.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_043.text: The sixth house was smaller than its booking board suggested. Two adjoining rooms had been closed for plaster work, but the booked passenger bench room remained admitted and dry. Cai checked the actual places before accepting the receipt. A late traveller wanted Zheng's near-door space because he disliked walking around other sleepers. Zheng needed the booked position for his own accepted movement arrangement. The keeper offered the late traveller a different available place at the posted rate. He accepted after complaining, and nobody asked Zheng to give up a real need for a stranger's convenience.

lantern_02_044.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_044.text: Yue sat in the courtyard after supper with her personal notebook. The old lens, cloth samples, sealed public packets, and private source wrapper all rested inside under different permissions. She drew their shapes without reproducing their unoffered contents. The rope maker's description had made her notice how many ordinary closures kept a journey possible. Each tie protected something; each tie could also make it harder to examine what lay beneath. She left the drawing as an observation, rather than turning the objects into an allegory their owners had never asked to inhabit.

lantern_02_045.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_045.text: Zheng joined her because the courtyard bench caught a little warmth from the kitchen wall. He asked about her prior realm examination. Yue described the recovered readings as prior results: seventy-two and three-eighths, seventy-two and a half, seventy-two and a quarter usable units after sampling, each within the named test's compatible limits. She had made no arrival measurement on this journey. His eyes brightened at the exact fractions. He had spent too many years hearing workers replace a measured limit with the word plenty when everybody wanted a job finished.

lantern_02_046.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_046.text: She kept the physical input ceiling separate from those reserves. The last cleared arrangement admitted a half unit over four ordinary breaths, no more than an eighth each breath, for a quarter unit of useful output through its prepared path. It required an independent stop and full grounded release. More stored reserve had not retested that ceiling. Zheng said a relay fuel cabinet could contain enough stones for a month while its next shutter still had to move within one small admitted interval. The likeness concerned a limit, not identical machinery.

lantern_02_047.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_047.text: Yue asked whether Chime had a qualified great-circuit examiner. Zheng knew Shao Ye at the ordinary training registry. She accepted registered workers under specific curriculum terms and rejected people who wanted a certificate by demonstrating exhaustion. He had seen her stop a trial when a student tried to repeat it with numb fingers. Yue wanted the address, not a promise of acceptance. Zheng gave the public address from his own correspondence book with its owner's admitted institutional contact. Its private letters stayed closed.

lantern_02_048.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_048.text: The Day 1397 approach inspection had passed under its current passenger limit. Cai checked the receiving time and began the last long road stage. The bank works narrowed one bend enough that passengers remained seated while the assigned road watcher guided the cart. A new retaining wall stood beside exposed earth from the repair. Yue could see the mason's stamped load notice, but not every foundation. She took the watcher and report within their actual scope. The cart moved slowly enough that everybody felt how much a safe turn could still demand attention.

lantern_02_049.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_049.text: Beyond the bend, a ground carrier passed in the opposite direction with Chime's public cancellation notice. He had a paid route, ordinary provisions, and a covered case fixed to his pack saddle. The lamp's closed window had not stopped every message; it had increased work and travel time for named alternatives. The carrier raised a hand to Cai and continued. Yue could not know whether he would arrive at each receiver on time. His actual departure made the alternative more than a comforting sentence on Deng's sheet.

lantern_02_050.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_050.text: They reached the seventh booked house before its kitchen's last meal issue. Cai delivered one admitted local notice packet and kept the Chime packet under its separate onward custody. The house clerk signed only the local count. Rui laid her cloth samples on the dry table and checked each wrapper after a week of carriage. None had opened. One outer corner had rubbed thin. She repaired that wrapper with her own purchased paper and recorded the change on the handling sheet. The cloth inside did not inherit damage merely because the cover needed work.

lantern_02_051.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_051.text: Zheng's niece had sent a message to the house welcoming him home on the expected day. It included no instruction to hurry through the road inspection. She had arranged an ordinary cart from Chime's receiving yard to his rented rooms, with its fee under their household account. Zheng looked pleased and slightly irritated by the arrangement. He could still walk locally, but wanted to arrive without carrying the lens through the freight crowd. He sent an actual acceptance through the house clerk, paying the ordinary charge from his own pouch.

lantern_02_052.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_052.text: Yue sent no second home letter yet. Her first remained in transit, and another brief position note would cost money without answering a new question. She kept a draft for Chime's actual arrival. Nan had given her the kitchen's receiving address if the journey failed before town. The address belonged to a former lodging relationship, not a free lifelong refuge. Yue hoped to send Nan a plain arrival line because she wanted to. The letter would be ordinary correspondence, with its own fee and receiver, after the journey had a result.

lantern_02_053.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_053.text: On Day 1398, Chime Reach appeared as roofs beneath a pale line of trees. The old relay tower stood above the association yard, shorter than Yue had imagined from the printed lamp emblem. A timber stair reached its inspection platform, while most work occupied the lower rooms. Cai stopped at the outer weigh strip and waited for the yard watcher. The passenger cart's arrival still needed its freight and people received. Yue had watched that distinction become three boxes and now saw the actual crowd that made shortcuts tempting.

lantern_02_054.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_054.text: Ma Yan met the cart with a covered counting slate. She received the sealed Chime notice packet under the association reference, checked its condition, and signed Cai's onward delivery line. The passengers unloaded only after the freight lane cleared. Zheng's niece, Zheng Bao, waited beside the ordinary hired household cart. She checked the supported lens case with her uncle before the driver took it. Yue helped hold the door when asked, leaving the lifting to the household arrangement's accepted carrier. A meeting at the yard had become an actual onward journey.

lantern_02_055.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_055.text: Rui's school receiver arrived with the purchasing clerk's written authority. They checked the cloth sample count and the repaired outer wrapper. The receiver accepted the samples for the named tests and signed their temporary school custody. Rui retained the owners' price cards until the purchasing sitting. She and the receiver walked toward the school lodging house, carrying the admitted case together. The cloth had arrived in time for its outdoor comparison. It had not yet passed, been purchased, or acquired permission for every classroom use.

lantern_02_056.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_056.text: Ma directed Yue to the traveller receiving desk. The desk confirmed the ticket's completed ordinary carriage and seven actual bench receipts. Its paid amount would be settled against the issuing station without another charge to Yue for the same seat. Passenger meals remained in her personal account. The clerk gave her the travel completion copy and asked whether she had a receiving appointment. Deng's proposal address named one, conditional on actual arrival. The clerk sent a short arrival notice through the association's internal runner, whose paid duty included that desk.

lantern_02_057.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_057.text: Yue booked two nights in a local workers' lodging house at two copper each, paid from her own money. The house accepted no association bill without an actual authorised appointment. Its keeper gave her a room key and showed the common washing hour. Yue wanted to sleep before reading more notices. She put the admitted source wrapper on the room's dry shelf, checked the lock with the keeper, and took a plain meal. Chime's relay light flashed once above the yard while she ate, serving work she had not yet been hired to perform.

lantern_02_058.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_058.text: On Day 1399, Yue delivered the food seller's notice request to Ma's public receiving counter. Ma read the current location and accepted it for the circulation review. She could not promise that the next print run would reach the stall before its budget and carrier list were checked. She gave Yue an actual request receipt. Yue paid the ordinary post fee she had agreed with Cai. The seller's request now had a responsible office, but its eventual answered need still remained separate from the receipt.

lantern_02_059.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_059.text: Deng offered a short arrival appointment for Day 1400. She had reserved no wages beyond the completed Wheatbridge comparison, and the proposed local work still required scope and acceptance. Yue brought the original receiving references and kept the private fields covered as before. The appointment could establish what the association needed, what records it owned, and which duties remained elsewhere. Her arrival supplied none of those answers automatically. She walked back through the public yard, watching ordinary porters receive packets beneath a lantern whose fuel cabinet stood firmly shut.

lantern_02_060.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_060.text: The school completed its sample tests before Rui's purchasing sitting on Day 1400. One dark cloth hid the classroom insects too well; the pale sample stained beyond the accepted washing method. The third met the school's recorded ordinary uses within its offered price. The purchasing clerk accepted a finite order, retaining the rejected samples for return to their owners. Rui received her completed travel allowance account and paid the unused balance back. The journey had enabled an actual choice rather than sold every sample.

lantern_02_061.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_061.text: Yue heard that result from Rui herself at the public meal table. Rui had permission to share the broad purchasing outcome, and chose to do so. The owners' price cards remained covered. She would return on her own booked school carriage after its receiving check, taking the two rejected samples under their actual wrappers. Yue wished her a sound journey. A practical acquaintance could end at a meal table without becoming a permanent claim on the next person's address or work.

lantern_02_062.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_062.text: At Deng's appointment, a relay shutter clicked twice beyond the inner partition. Jin Lu, the licensed isolation examiner, called a stop before a porter lifted the next admission tray. Nobody asked Yue to hold the shutter with personal qi. The queued packets stayed with their present custodians while Jin checked the affected assembly. Deng moved the appointment to the ordinary records room, whose table remained available. The service interruption had created delay before anybody at their table tried to make delay look complete.

lantern_02_063.speaker: narrator
lantern_02_063.text: Deng showed Yue the Six-Reach association's charter. Six named settlements funded this local service and its recorded carrier alternatives. Their boundaries began here; they did not annex the older mountain, river, archive, or basin institutions Yue had visited. She copied the public scope heading for tomorrow's proposed work and left the private annexes closed. The next question concerned which duties that small charter actually bought.
